component.name: InDuckGo
component.summary: Privacy-first browser with DuckDuckGo's tracker protections

description.p: InDuckGo is a WebKitGTK web browser that blocks third-party trackers with DuckDuckGo's open-source protections, upgrades connections to HTTPS, removes tracking parameters from links and announces Global Privacy Control. It has no extension support, by design.
Every profile and every site installed as an app runs in its own process with its own cookies and storage, so a link clicked in the browser never reaches the session of your bank or mailbox.

The Tor window browses through InDuckGo's own Tor, never a system-wide one. Its session lives in memory only, WebRTC is off, onion services open directly, and bridges (Snowflake, obfs4 or your own) reach Tor where it is blocked. New Identity deletes the session and switches to new Tor circuits.
InDuckGo is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Duck Duck Go, Inc.
The WebKitGTK browser behaves as in 1.2.0. The shared core gained tab placement, window button style and profile tile preferences for the upcoming Qt edition, which is not packaged yet.
Interface texts for the new features were added to all translations.
The WebKitGTK browser behaves as in 1.1.2. The shared core gained the groundwork of the upcoming Qt edition, which is not packaged yet.
Interface texts for the new features were added to all translations.
Smooth mouse-wheel scrolling: every wheel step is animated like in Chromium, with a switch in the preferences.
Faster scrolling on pages with scroll animations.
Interface language: choose among 68 languages in the preferences.
Downloads: a list in the toolbar, a choice of save folder, a clear-list button and a manager with the whole history.
Faster pages: drawing with GTK's OpenGL renderer instead of copying every frame through memory.
Tor window: browsing through InDuckGo's own Tor, with bridges, onion services and New Identity.
Toolbar: an onion button for the Tor window, and preferences to choose the toolbar's buttons.
